update.title: New version available: {version}
update.description: A new version of TetraControl2Connect is available. Please update the application to benefit from the latest features and bug fixes.

setup.title: Initial setup required
setup.description: TetraControl and Connect are not configured yet. The setup wizard guides you through the basic configuration in a few steps.

backups.subtitle: Restore points for the settings

info.automatic: Whenever the settings are changed, a daily backup is created automatically (one per day). You can also create a manual backup at any time.
info.restore: Use {action} to reset all settings to an earlier point in time. The current configuration will be completely replaced by the backed-up values.

empty.title: No backups available
empty.description: Backups are created automatically as soon as you change settings.

backups.created: A manual backup was created successfully.

severity.info: Translate the severity levels from TETRA alarm messages into readable labels for Feuer Software Connect.
severity.infoDetail: The {key} is the severity value from the TETRA message; the {value} is the text displayed in Connect. Optionally, the translation can also be used as the incident keyword.
severity.useAsKeywordHint: Translated severity levels are used as the incident keyword

sirenCallout.info: Configure the translation of siren alarm codes. When a siren receives an alarm code, it is converted into readable text using the configured translations.
sirenCallout.infoDetail: The {key} is the numeric code from the TETRA message; the {value} is the text displayed in Connect. Optionally, the translation can be used as the incident keyword.
sirenCallout.useAsKeyword: Use siren code translation as keyword
sirenCallout.useAsKeywordHint: Translated siren codes are used as the incident keyword

sirenStatus.info: Translate the error codes reported by sirens when a fault occurs. These translations turn technical error codes into readable descriptions for Feuer Software Connect.
sirenStatus.infoDetail: The {key} is the numeric code from the siren status message; the {value} is the error description shown in Connect as a fault message.

pattern.subtitle: Regex patterns for alarm parsing

intro.text: Define the regular expressions (regex) used to extract information from TETRA alarm messages (SDS). Each field needs a regex pattern that extracts the desired value from the alarm text.
intro.usage: Use {namedGroups} such as {example} to mark the extracted value. You can check your patterns directly with the {tester} or have suggestions generated via the {aiHelp}.

tester.title: Regex Tester
tester.samplePlaceholder: Paste a sample alarm text here to test the patterns...
tester.sampleHint: This text is used to test all patterns and for the AI assistant. Click the flask icon next to a pattern to see the result.

pattern.invalidPatternCannotTest: The pattern is invalid and cannot be tested.

numberPattern.label: Incident number
numberPattern.hint: e.g. a sequential number such as "E2024-001234"

reporterPhoneNumberPattern.label: Reporter phone number
reporterPhoneNumberPattern.hint: Phone number of the person reporting

cityPattern.label: City
cityPattern.hint: Name of the incident location's city

streetPattern.label: Street
streetPattern.hint: Street name of the incident location

houseNumberPattern.label: House number
houseNumberPattern.hint: House number at the incident location

zipCodePattern.label: ZIP code
zipCodePattern.hint: Postal code of the incident location

ai.title: AI Regex Assistant
ai.expectedValueDescription: Which value should be extracted for "{field}" from the sample text?
ai.expectedValuePlaceholder: e.g. paste the actual value from the sample text above here
ai.privacy: I confirm that the sample text contains {noSensitiveData}. The text will be sent to an external AI service.
ai.promptCopiedDescription: Paste the prompt into your preferred AI tool (e.g. Gemini, Claude, Copilot).
ai.copiedDescription: AI prompt was copied to the clipboard.

prompt.intro: I need a regular expression (regex) that extracts a specific value from a TETRA radio alarm message (SDS).
prompt.task: Create a regex pattern that extracts the value for the field "{field}" from the following alarm text.
prompt.expected: In the sample text, the value for "{field}" is: {value}
prompt.structureHeading: Important notes on the message structure
prompt.structureSeparators: The alarm text follows a fixed structure with separators (e.g. line breaks, semicolons, tabs or other delimiters)
prompt.structureExample: The given value "{value}" is only an example from this particular message. In other messages, a different value appears at the same position (e.g. instead of "{value}" there could be completely different text)
prompt.structurePosition: The pattern must identify the **position of the value within the message structure**, not the specific value itself
prompt.structureOrientation: Use the surrounding separators, keywords or the field position to target the correct section
prompt.requirementRobust: The pattern should be robust and also match slightly different values at the same position
prompt.requirementOutput: Return only the final regex pattern, without code blocks or explanation

connect.subtitle: Manage sites, subnet addresses and sirens

info.sites: Manage your Feuer Software Connect sites here. Each site represents a Connect instance with its own API-Key.
info.subnets: {sna} assign TETRA subnets to a site. If “Alarm directly” is enabled, alarms are forwarded to this site immediately. The {gssi} is the group address of the subnet.
info.sirens: {sirens} are identified by their ISSI. Optionally, a heartbeat interval can be configured to monitor the siren's availability.

tetracontrol.subtitle: Connection settings for the TetraControl server

info.connection: Configure the connection to the TetraControl server here. TetraControl2Connect connects to TetraControl via WebSocket and receives status, position and SDS messages in real time.
info.host: Enter the IP address or hostname of the TetraControl server and the WebSocket port.

info.dataForwarding: Define which data is forwarded from TetraControl to Feuer Software Connect. Individual features such as vehicle status, position transmission, alarms or user availability can be enabled or disabled independently.
info.parameters: Under {numbers} and {timespans} you can adjust timeout and retry parameters. The {heartbeat} periodically sends a signal to a configurable URL to monitor the system's availability.

acceptSDSAsCalloutsWithPattern.label: Accept SDS as callout with pattern

info.definition: Define the TETRA status values that correspond to the various availability states in Feuer Software Connect.
info.matching: When a user changes their status on the TETRA radio, the numeric status value is matched against this table and the corresponding availability status is sent to Connect. Enter the status numbers as comma-separated values (e.g. “1,2”).

limitedAvailableStatus.label: Limited availability
limitedAvailableStatus.description: Status value for responders with limited availability

comingStatus.label: Coming
comingStatus.description: Status value for responders who confirmed

notComingStatus.label: Not coming
notComingStatus.description: Status value for responders who declined

comingLaterStatus.label: Coming later
comingLaterStatus.description: Status value for responders who confirmed with a delay

welcome.title: Welcome to TetraControl2Connect!
welcome.intro: This wizard guides you through the initial setup. In just a few steps you will connect TetraControl to Feuer Software Connect.

tetracontrol.title: TetraControl connection
tetracontrol.description: Configure the WebSocket connection to the TetraControl server.
tetracontrol.hostDescription: IP address or hostname of the TetraControl server

connect.title: First Connect site
connect.description: Add your first Feuer Software Connect site. You can add more sites later in the settings.
connect.siteNameDescription: A descriptive name for the site
connect.apiKeyPlaceholder: API key from Feuer Software Connect
connect.apiKeyDescription: You can find the API key in the {portal} under "Öffentliche Connect-Schnittstelle" (public Connect interface).
connect.info: Each site requires its own API key from Feuer Software Connect. You can configure subnet addresses (SNA/GSSI) and sirens afterwards in the detailed settings.

options.description: Choose which data should be sent to Connect.
options.alarmsWarning: {important} For operations from SDS messages to be detected correctly and sent to Connect, you must configure the matching regex patterns under {pattern} after the initial setup.
options.alarmsWarningDetails: These patterns determine how the operation number, keyword, address and other information are extracted from the alarm text. Without configured patterns, received alarms cannot be evaluated.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Review your settings and save the configuration.

completed.title: Setup complete!
completed.description: The basic configuration has been saved. You can now adjust further settings or return to the dashboard.
completed.nextStepPattern: Configure regex patterns so that alarms from SDS messages can be evaluated (operation number, keyword, address, etc.)
completed.nextStepSubnetAddresses: Add SNA/GSSI mappings for the site
completed.nextStepStatusMappings: Map TETRA status codes to Connect status values

toast.completedDescription: All settings have been saved. You can adjust the configuration at any time via the settings pages.
